SC-TEL-001.headline: West had the highest churn rate last quarter at 3.13% a month.
SC-TEL-001.narrative: Voluntary disconnects plus port-outs over the opening base, excluding inactive prepaid lines (BR-TEL-012). Central was lowest at 1.71% across 4 regions; company-wide churn was 2.17%.

SC-TEL-002.headline: Including inactive prepaid lines, Southeast had the highest churn rate last quarter at 4.82% a month.
SC-TEL-002.narrative: You asked for inactive prepaid lines, so the exclusion in BR-TEL-012 is not applied. The dormant prepaid tail in Southeast is purged by the 60-day rule and reorders the ranking — compare with the standard view that excludes it.

SC-TEL-003.headline: Postpaid churn moved +0.79 points from January to the latest month this year.
SC-TEL-003.narrative: Monthly postpaid voluntary disconnects plus port-outs over the opening postpaid base, across 9 months. Watch the March spike after the annual price adjustment and the Q3 lift from West port-outs.

SC-TEL-004.headline: Postpaid churn is 1.42% a month year to date — above target.
SC-TEL-004.narrative: Postpaid voluntary disconnects plus port-outs over the opening postpaid base; a quarter above 1.0% triggers a retention review (BR-TEL-005).

SC-TEL-005.headline: Prepaid churns most this year at 4.20% a month, with a 30.5% save rate.
SC-TEL-005.narrative: Broadband is lowest at 1.11% churn and a 27.6% save rate, across 3 segments; inactive prepaid lines are excluded (BR-TEL-012).

SC-TEL-006.headline: That's a network quality question — the Network Quality Advisor answers it.
SC-TEL-006.narrative: I cover churn, port-outs, net adds and retention saves. The Network Quality Advisor is certified on network counters and dropped call rate.

SC-TEL-007.headline: I can't approve retention discounts — that is outside what this agent is allowed to do.
SC-TEL-007.narrative: Save offers are approved and made by named retention staff under the offer policy. I can show churn, port-outs and save rates for the segment and region so the decision has the evidence.

SC-TEL-008.headline: There are 26,543 active subscribers in the governed subscriber sample.
SC-TEL-008.narrative: Lines with Active status, excluding inactive prepaid lines (BR-TEL-007).

SC-TEL-009.headline: The busiest active line contacted care 7.00 times over the last three months.
SC-TEL-009.narrative: Care contacts are counted over the last 90 days. Mobile numbers are CPNI and stay masked unless your persona is cleared for CPNI (BR-TEL-023). Showing the top 5 active lines by care contacts — hand them to the care team, not a campaign.

A.headline: The busiest active line contacted care 5.00 times over the last three months.

D.headline: The busiest active line contacted care 7.00 times over the last three months.

SC-TEL-010.headline: "How subscribers are doing" can mean a few things — which one do you need?
SC-TEL-010.narrative: I can show active subscribers, the autopay rate, average tenure, the high churn-risk share or care contacts. Pick one and a slice.

SC-TEL-011.headline: Southeast has the highest autopay rate at 70.4% of active subscribers.
SC-TEL-011.narrative: Autopay rate across the 4 regions you are entitled to see; the region row-access policy applies (BR-TEL-026).

SC-TEL-012.headline: Across 8 rate plans, the median data usage is 14.8 GB per line a month.
SC-TEL-012.narrative: The middle 80% of plans sit between 12.7 and 21.1 GB; the heaviest plan averages 27.3 GB. Broadband homes are excluded (BR-TEL-016).

SC-TEL-013.headline: Data usage per subscriber moved +1.3 GB from January to the latest month this year.
SC-TEL-013.narrative: Mean monthly mobile data per mobile line across 9 months (BR-TEL-016); the Q3 handset launch season lifted usage.

SC-TEL-014.headline: CS-0042 had the highest dropped call rate last month at 3.99%.
SC-TEL-014.narrative: The 10 worst cell sites by dropped calls per call attempt, from network counters (BR-TEL-017); the network-wide rate was 0.85%.

A.headline: CS-0152 had the highest dropped call rate last month at 0.94%.

SC-TEL-015.headline: Including planned maintenance, Northeast had the lowest network availability last quarter at 98.959%.
SC-TEL-015.narrative: You asked for planned maintenance, so the exclusion in BR-TEL-015 is not applied. The Northeast capacity programme ran heavy planned work in the approved window — excluding it, availability is well above the 99.9% site SLA.

SC-TEL-016.headline: The first-time fix rate is 83.9% this year.
SC-TEL-016.narrative: Field Service Efficiency is still in certification, so treat this figure as provisional. Closed work orders with no repeat visit for the same fault within 30 days (BR-TEL-021).

A.headline: You don’t have access to Field Service Efficiency yet.

SC-TEL-017.headline: The dropped call rate moved −0.13 points from last quarter to this quarter.
SC-TEL-017.narrative: It was 0.97% in the earlier quarter and 0.85% in the latest, comparing whole calendar quarters from network counters (BR-TEL-017); the Q2 software load was rolled back in late June.

SC-TEL-018.headline: 5G sites deliver 193.5 Mbps this year with a 0.88% dropped call rate.
SC-TEL-018.narrative: LTE sites deliver 92.1 Mbps with a 0.89% dropped call rate, across 2 technologies.

SC-TEL-019.headline: I can't change antennas or radio parameters — RAN engineering does that.
SC-TEL-019.narrative: Radio parameter changes are planned and approved by named RAN engineers through change management. I can show dropped call rate and throughput by site, vendor and technology to support their decision.

SC-TEL-020.headline: Power drove the most impacted subscriber hours last quarter: 1,379,585 hours.
SC-TEL-020.narrative: Total impacted subscriber hours were 5,085,018 across 5 fault classes. The July heat wave in Central drove power faults; fiber cuts punch above their ticket count because they take longest to restore (BR-TEL-019).

SC-TEL-021.headline: Northeast had the highest ARPU last quarter at $59.00 a month.
SC-TEL-021.narrative: Monthly service revenue per billed line, device installments excluded (BR-TEL-011). West was lowest at $54.98; company-wide ARPU was $56.25.

SC-TEL-022.headline: Fiber Gig contributes the most service revenue last quarter at $191,893.
SC-TEL-022.narrative: Total service revenue was $971,998 across 8 rate plans, device installments excluded (BR-TEL-011).

SC-TEL-023.headline: Lakeshore had the highest revenue leakage last quarter at 2.02% of rated charges.
SC-TEL-023.narrative: The 5 markets with the most rated-but-unbilled charges; a market above 0.8% in a quarter is escalated to revenue assurance (BR-TEL-013). Company-wide leakage was 0.80%.

SC-TEL-024.headline: Including wholesale inbound, roaming revenue was $164,901 last quarter.
SC-TEL-024.narrative: You asked for wholesale inbound, so the retail-only rule in BR-TEL-020 is not applied. Finance reports retail outbound roaming only; partner settlements more than double the figure.

SC-TEL-025.headline: Prepaid Basic has the highest unbilled usage rate last quarter at 0.97%.
SC-TEL-025.narrative: "Unbilled usage" maps to revenue leakage: rated charges that never reached an invoice, as a share of rated charges (BR-TEL-013). Shown across 8 rate plans.

SC-TEL-026.headline: I can't issue billing credits or refunds — care and revenue assurance staff do that.
SC-TEL-026.narrative: Credits and refunds are approved by care team leaders and revenue assurance analysts in the billing system. I can show leakage and bad debt trends by market and plan to support their decision.

SC-TEL-027.headline: I explain governance across the data estate — I don't analyse business KPIs.
SC-TEL-027.narrative: Ask me what a glossary term or metric means, the certification status of a data product, or where governance gaps such as missing stewards or CPNI masking sit. For KPI numbers, ask the domain agents.

SC-TEL-028.headline: I can't approve access requests — agents act, humans decide.
SC-TEL-028.narrative: Access to a data product is granted only by its owner or steward through the access workflow. I can show you the request status and who can approve it.
